records.literal_gloss: And called Jacob to his sons and said, gather yourselves, that I may tell you what will befall you in [the] end of the days.

en.L: And Jacob called his sons and said, "Gather yourselves together, so that I may tell you what will happen to you in the end of the days."
en.B: Jacob summoned his sons and said, "Come together, and I will tell you what lies ahead for you in the time to come."
en.R: Jacob sent for his sons and said, "Come near, and I will tell you what is going to happen to you in the years ahead."

es.L: Y llamó Jacob a sus hijos y dijo: «{{plural_you:Reúnanse|Reuníos}}, para que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} anuncie lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} sucederá al final de los días».

fr.L: Et Jacob appela ses fils et dit : « Rassemblez-vous, afin que je vous annonce ce qui vous arrivera à la fin des jours. »
fr.B: Jacob fit venir ses fils et leur dit : « Réunissez-vous, et je vous dirai ce qui vous attend dans les temps à venir. »
fr.R: Jacob a appelé ses fils et leur a dit : « Approchez-vous. Je vais vous dire ce qui va vous arriver dans les années qui viennent. »

ko.B: 야곱이 아들들을 불러 놓고 말하였다. "모두 모여라. 앞으로 너희에게 닥칠 일을 내가 너희에게 일러 주겠다."

pt.B: Jacó chamou os seus filhos e disse: "Venham todos juntos, e eu lhes direi o que espera por vocês no tempo que está por vir."
pt.R: Jacó mandou chamar os seus filhos e disse: "Cheguem perto, e eu vou contar a vocês o que vai acontecer com vocês nos anos que vêm pela frente."

decisions.choice: the end of the days: the time to come
alternatives: the last days of the world
decisions.reason: The phrase looks ahead to a later time, here the days when the sons have become tribes in the land. The prophets use the same words for the time when God brings his purposes to their goal (Isaiah 2:2; Hosea 3:5).

decisions.choice: a father's last words
decisions.reason: As Isaac had done (27:1-4), the dying head of the family speaks words over his sons that shape their future.

decisions.choice: in the end of the days
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase; Balanced and Readable say what it means here (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: al final de los días
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase in plain modern Spanish rather than the older "postreros"; Balanced and Readable say what it means here, as the English does.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("appela", "fit venir"); passé composé at Readable ("a appelé"); Jacob's sayings keep the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. Verses 2-27 are Jacob's poetry, so they are speech throughout.

decisions.choice: "trong những ngày sau cùng" (L) for "in the end of the days"
decisions.reason: The time to come (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, Balanced and Readable say the plain sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Jacob's sayings (verses 1-27) are in the plain style (해라체) a father uses to his sons, with no archaic endings
decisions.reason: The terms note sets the plain style for a parent to his children, and the Korean style guide keeps the older biblical endings out of a modern translation even in poetry. Like the English, the Korean is set as prose, not in lines.

decisions.choice: vocês to the sons together, você to each son (verses 1-27)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter: Jacob speaks to his sons as people speak to one another, "vocês" to them all and "você" to each son he addresses (Reuben, Judah, Joseph), at every level, also in the poetry of verses 2-27; "vós" and "tu" would sound archaic or like prayer (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4). He says "tu" only to God, in verse 18. Literal keeps "no fim dos dias" (m1).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Amharic. This holds for the prayer in verse 18.

decisions.choice: Jacob's blessings are poetry
decisions.reason: From here to verse 27 Jacob speaks in poetry, in pairs of lines where the second says the first again in other words: "sons of Jacob" and "Israel your father". Several sayings play on the meaning of a son's name. Many lines are rare or hard words, so a number of readings are uncertain.

decisions.choice: Jacob ... Israel: one man, two names
decisions.reason: The parallel lines use both of the patriarch's names (32:28); his sons will become the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: Jacob to his sons in the blessings: "con" / "các con" to the one addressed; "nó" where he speaks of a son in the pictures of animals
decisions.reason: The blessings are a father's last words (meaning decision), so the family words stay; the poem's turns between "you" and "he" are kept.

decisions.choice: Jacob speaks to his sons with "እናንተ" and to each son with "አንተ"; the poem is set as running sentences
alternatives: poetic line breaks in Amharic only
decisions.reason: A father to his sons uses the familiar "you". The English levels of this chapter carry no line markers, so neither does the Amharic; the poetry is carried by short clauses joined with "፤".

records.literal_gloss: Reuben, my firstborn [are] you, my strength and [the] first of my vigor, excess of dignity and excess of power.

en.L: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the first of my vigor, preeminent in dignity and preeminent in power.
en.B: Reuben, my firstborn, you are my strength, the first child of my vigor, standing above the rest in honor, above the rest in power.
en.R: Reuben, you are my oldest son. You were born when I was young and strong. As my firstborn you had the first place in honor and in power.

pt.B: Rúben, meu primogênito, você é a minha força, o primeiro filho do meu vigor, o que está acima dos outros em honra, acima dos outros em poder.
pt.R: Rúben, você é o meu filho mais velho. Você nasceu quando eu era jovem e forte. Como meu primogênito, você tinha o primeiro lugar em honra e em poder.
